Hi Tom and Priya,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great visibility into the checkout fraud use case. I promised a short, focused follow-up with the recommendation and concrete next steps based on the latency and throughput numbers you shared.

Quick summary of your requirements from the call:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,800
- Typical QPS: 120–180 overall, with brief spikes up to ~320 QPS for 30–90 seconds during promos
- Latency target: P95 <= 120 ms for inference (end-to-end target includes network hops)
- Data residency: US-only; no requirement for on-prem currently
- Security: standard SOC2 + enterprise contract needed

Scorecard (short):
- Hosted API: Pros: fastest onboarding, auto-scaling, cost-effective for bursty workloads; Cons: multi-tenant limits on strict P95 guarantees during extreme bursts unless reserved concurrency is added
- Dedicated capacity (Reserved GPUs): Pros: predictable tail latency, isolation for caching/KV; Cons: higher baseline cost, longer provisioning lead time for >16 GPUs
- Private VPC/On‑Prem: Pros: full isolation, custom network topology; Cons: likely unnecessary now given US-only and no regulatory block; introduces procurement timeline and infra ops overhead

Recommendation: given your P95 target and burst profile, we recommend starting on Hosted API with a Dedicated reserve for steady-state capacity (mixed approach). Specifically:
- Reserve a modest dedicated pool sized for 120 QPS baseline (estimated 6 GPUs with our medium-quantized profile)
- Let Hosted API handle autoscaling for bursts up to 320 QPS; configure a burst budget and AI-rate policies so we have graceful scaling and cost controls
- If network hop adds >20–30 ms in your infra, consider moving to Dedicated-only for strict tail guarantees after the pilot

Attachments: I attached a one-page scorecard and a proposed load test plan that maps throughput/latency targets to a short 48-hour pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) RetailX to confirm: acceptance to run the 48-hour pilot (we’ll need an API key + expected test windows)
2) Redwood to schedule a joint load-test kickoff (Marissa will own execution)
3) Agree on success criteria for pilot: sustained P95 <= 120 ms at 180 QPS with controlled bursts to 320 QPS, and no >5% error rate

If that sounds good I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute kickoff and share the test plan details.

Best,

Thanks — putting together the concrete sizing notes for the pilot. Quick thoughts:
- Baseline reserve: 6 x A40-equivalent or 4 x A100-equivalent (depending on model quantization). I prefer the A100 path for headroom but call it out as an ops/contract implication.
- Autoscaling thresholds: configure for 150 QPS sustained, scale up aggressively at 200 QPS with cooldown 30s.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for inferred sessions — this should shave ~20 ms on average per request in our sims.
- Fallback behavior: configure automatic model downgrade to a smaller quantized variant with consistent sampling when capacity constrained. Also enable a short-lived queue (5s) before rejecting to smooth bursts.

I’ll attach a quick checklist for the pilot run and the load script parameters. We should be able to stand up the reserved pool within 72 hours after the PO.
